sides.text: Design only, make for others, or do both

more.text: Fabless firms (Qualcomm, NVIDIA, AMD, Apple) design chips and outsource manufacturing. Foundries (TSMC, GlobalFoundries) fabricate for others. Integrated device manufacturers (Intel, Samsung, Texas Instruments, Micron) design and make their own.

sides.text: Which business model does NVIDIA follow?

more.text: Fabless.
Founded in 1987 by Morris Chang in Taiwan. Manufactures leading-edge chips for companies such as Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, and Qualcomm.

sides.text: Which company pioneered the pure-play foundry model in 1987?

more.text: TSMC, founded by Morris Chang.

sides.text: Memory leader and a major foundry

more.text: A leading maker of DRAM and NAND flash, plus Samsung Foundry. Also makes phones, TVs, and displays.

sides.text: Which company is both a top memory maker and a foundry?

more.text: Samsung Electronics.
Founded in 1968 by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore. Designs and manufactures x86 CPUs and has expanded into manufacturing chips for other companies.
Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore.

sides.text: A foundry spun out of AMD in 2009

more.text: Focuses on mature and specialty nodes for automotive, IoT, and RF rather than the leading edge.

sides.text: Which foundry was spun out of AMD?

more.text: GlobalFoundries.
Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, mainly making mature and mid-range process nodes.

sides.text: Which Chinese company is the country's largest foundry?

more.text: SMIC.
A Dutch company based in Veldhoven. It's the sole supplier of EUV scanners, which are essential for the most advanced chips.

sides.text: Which company is the only supplier of EUV lithography machines?

more.text: ASML.

sides.text: Chip equipment: deposition, etch, and more

more.text: A US company that supplies equipment for depositing films, etching, ion implantation, and inspection.

sides.text: Which US company is the largest supplier of chip-making equipment overall?

more.text: Applied Materials.
Its tools etch and deposit the thin films that form transistor structures.

sides.text: Which company is best known for etch equipment, Lam Research or ASML?

more.text: Lam Research (ASML is known for lithography).
Finds defects and measures features on wafers and masks, which is crucial for yield.

sides.text: Which company focuses on wafer inspection and metrology?

more.text: KLA.
Makes coater/developers, etchers, and other fab equipment.

sides.text: Which Japanese company is a major supplier of fab equipment?

more.text: Tokyo Electron.
A UK-based company whose low-power cores power most smartphones, Apple's M-series, and many microcontrollers (Cortex-M). It licenses designs rather than selling chips.

sides.text: Which company licenses the CPU architecture used in most smartphones?

more.text: Arm.
Electronic design automation software is used to design, simulate, and verify chips and boards. These three dominate the market.

sides.text: Which type of software do Synopsys and Cadence sell?

more.text: Electronic design automation (EDA).
Makes DRAM and NAND flash. With Samsung and SK hynix it supplies most of the world's DRAM.

sides.text: Which US company is a major DRAM and NAND maker?

more.text: Micron.
A major DRAM and NAND supplier and a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used with AI accelerators.

sides.text: Which type of memory is stacked beside AI accelerators?

more.text: HBM (high-bandwidth memory).

sides.text: 300 mm for leading edge, 200 mm for analog and power

more.text: Larger wafers cut cost per die. Many analog, power, and sensor chips still use 200 mm fabs.

sides.text: Which wafer size is standard for leading-edge fabs?

more.text: Names like 5 nm or 3 nm no longer match a physical dimension. Compare density and performance instead.

sides.text: Does a 3 nm node have a 3 nm transistor feature?

more.text: No. The node name is a marketing label.
Companies such as ASE and Amkor package and test chips after the fab. Advanced packaging is a growing part of the business.
Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test.

sides.text: US funding for domestic chip manufacturing

more.text: Signed in August 2022, it provides about $52 billion in incentives for semiconductor manufacturing and research.

sides.text: Which 2022 US law funds domestic chip manufacturing?

more.text: The CHIPS and Science Act.
The M1 (2020) moved Macs from Intel to Apple-designed Arm chips, manufactured by TSMC. Apple is fabless.
TSMC.
Based in Dallas. Large analog portfolio and microcontrollers. Jack Kilby built the first integrated circuit there in 1958. Acquired National Semiconductor in 2011.

sides.text: Where did Jack Kilby build the first integrated circuit?

more.text: Texas Instruments.
Known for data converters and signal-chain chips. Acquired Linear Technology in 2017 and Maxim Integrated in 2021.

sides.text: Which company acquired Linear Technology in 2017?

more.text: Analog Devices.
A Dutch company spun out of Philips Semiconductors in 2006. Merged with Freescale in 2015. Strong in automotive and NFC.

sides.text: Which company was spun out of Philips Semiconductors?

more.text: NXP.
A Franco-Italian company. STM32 is one of the most widely used Arm Cortex-M microcontroller families.

sides.text: Which company makes the STM32 family?

more.text: STMicroelectronics.
Acquired Atmel in 2016, bringing the AVR chips used on classic Arduino boards.

sides.text: Which company owns the AVR line used in the Arduino Uno?

more.text: Microchip Technology (via Atmel).
Formed from Hitachi, Mitsubishi, and NEC chip businesses. A leading automotive microcontroller supplier.

sides.text: Which Japanese company is a major automotive microcontroller maker?

more.text: Renesas.
A German company that leads in power MOSFETs, IGBTs, and silicon carbide. Also makes the AURIX automotive microcontrollers.

sides.text: Which German company is a leader in power semiconductors?

more.text: Infineon.
A Norwegian company whose nRF52 series appears in many BLE products.

sides.text: Which company's nRF52 chips are common in BLE devices?

more.text: Nordic Semiconductor.
A Chinese company whose low-cost chips drove the growth of DIY and commercial IoT.
Espressif.
A fabless company known for Snapdragon processors, 5G modems, and a large wireless patent portfolio. Co-founded in 1985 by Irwin Jacobs, Andrew Viterbi, and others.

sides.text: Which company's Snapdragon chips power many Android phones?

more.text: Qualcomm.

sides.text: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, networking, and broadband chips

more.text: Also supplied the SoCs in Raspberry Pi boards.

sides.text: Which company made the main chips in early Raspberry Pi boards?

more.text: Broadcom.
Strong in automotive power chips and image sensors, including silicon carbide products.

sides.text: Which type of sensor chip is onsemi well known for?

more.text: Image sensors (and power chips).
FreeRTOS is widely used and maintained by AWS. Zephyr is an open-source RTOS under the Linux Foundation. Yocto and Buildroot build embedded Linux images.

sides.text: Which open-source RTOS is hosted by the Linux Foundation?

more.text: Zephyr.
Tier-1 suppliers build ECUs, sensors, and modules for carmakers. Vehicles contain many dozens of ECUs on CAN and automotive Ethernet.

sides.text: What is a company that supplies modules directly to carmakers called?

more.text: A Tier-1 supplier.
A non-profit that governs the RISC-V instruction set. SiFive and others sell RISC-V cores.
Governing the open RISC-V instruction set.
Founded by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem. GeForce GPUs for gaming, and CUDA for general-purpose computing that later made it central to AI.

sides.text: Which company created the CUDA programming platform?

more.text: NVIDIA.
Ryzen CPUs and Radeon GPUs. Designs semi-custom chips for PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

sides.text: Which company designs the chips in both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X?

more.text: AMD.

sides.text: PS5 uses a custom AMD chip

more.text: PlayStation 5 (2020) uses a custom AMD Zen 2 CPU and RDNA 2 GPU, with a very fast SSD.

sides.text: Which company makes the PS5's processor?

more.text: AMD (custom design).

sides.text: Xbox Series X and S use custom AMD chips

more.text: Microsoft's consoles share an AMD Zen 2 and RDNA 2 architecture with the PS5, with different configurations.

sides.text: Which architecture do both the Xbox Series X and PS5 CPUs use?

more.text: AMD Zen 2.

sides.text: A hybrid handheld powered by NVIDIA

more.text: The original Switch (2017) used a custom NVIDIA Tegra chip. Nintendo favors efficient hardware over raw power.

sides.text: Which company supplied the original Nintendo Switch's processor?

more.text: NVIDIA.
Launched in 2022 with a custom AMD processor, running a Linux-based SteamOS.

sides.text: Which operating system does the Steam Deck use?

more.text: A Linux-based SteamOS.

sides.text: Many simple cores vs a few complex ones

more.text: GPUs run thousands of threads in parallel, ideal for graphics and matrix math. CPUs excel at serial, branching work.

sides.text: Why are GPUs good at graphics and AI?

more.text: They run many threads in parallel.
Gaming volume funded GPU research. The same parallel architecture later accelerated scientific computing and AI.

sides.text: What technology originally built for games now powers AI training?

more.text: The GPU.
NVIDIA introduced consumer ray tracing cores in its RTX GPUs in 2018. AMD and Intel added similar hardware.

sides.text: Which year did NVIDIA's RTX GPUs bring ray tracing to consumers?

more.text: GDDR is cost-effective and high bandwidth for gaming cards. HBM is stacked for far higher bandwidth, used in data center accelerators.

sides.text: Which memory is stacked beside AI accelerators?

more.text: HBM.
Entered the gaming GPU market in 2022 with the Arc series.

sides.text: Which company launched the Arc series of gaming GPUs?

more.text: Intel.
Meta's Quest headsets use Qualcomm Snapdragon XR chips. Phones game on Snapdragon and Apple A-series chips.

sides.text: Which chip family powers Meta Quest headsets?

more.text: Qualcomm Snapdragon XR.
First launched in 2012 by the Raspberry Pi Foundation in the UK to teach computing. Runs Linux. Pi 4 arrived in 2019 and Pi 5 in 2023. Its RP2040 chip (2021) powers the Pico.

sides.text: Which chip powers the Raspberry Pi Pico?

more.text: The RP2040.
Began in 2005 in Ivrea, Italy, for design students. The Uno uses an ATmega328P. Huge library and shield ecosystem.

sides.text: In which country did Arduino begin?

more.text: Italy.
Founded in 2005 by Limor Fried. Known for tutorials, CircuitPython, and breakout boards.
Limor Fried.
Founded in 2003 by Nathan Seidle. Sells breakout boards and kits and publishes open hardware.
Boulder, Colorado.
Designs and manufactures development boards and offers fabrication services.

sides.text: In which Chinese city is Seeed Studio based?

more.text: Shenzhen.

sides.text: Open-source Linux boards with real-time units

more.text: BeagleBoard.org's boards include programmable real-time units (PRUs) for tight timing alongside Linux.
Real-time I/O alongside Linux.
MicroPython runs Python on small chips. CircuitPython is Adafruit's beginner-friendly fork.

sides.text: Which language do MicroPython and CircuitPython use?

more.text: Python.
Started by Jean-Pierre Charras and now supported by a community and CERN. Used by hobbyists and professionals.

sides.text: What is a free open-source tool for designing PCBs?

more.text: KiCad.
Online fabs make small PCB runs cheaply, often with assembly. Upload Gerber files and receive boards in days.

sides.text: What file format do PCB fabs usually need?

more.text: Gerber files.
Distributors stock thousands of parts with datasheets and parametric search. LCSC pairs with JLCPCB assembly.

sides.text: Where do hobbyists commonly buy electronic parts?

more.text: Distributors such as Digi-Key and Mouser.

sides.text: Designs published for anyone to build

more.text: The OSHWA certification marks projects that publish design files under open licenses.
Design files so anyone can build or modify it.

sides.text: 3D printers, laser cutters, and shared tools

more.text: Fast iteration with printed enclosures and breadboards before a custom PCB.

sides.text: Why use a 3D-printed enclosure when prototyping?

more.text: To iterate on the physical design quickly and cheaply.
Home batteries (Powerwall) and utility-scale batteries (Megapack), plus solar products.

sides.text: Which Tesla product is a utility-scale battery?

more.text: The Megapack.

sides.text: The world's largest EV battery maker

more.text: A Chinese company that makes LFP and NMC cells for many automakers.

sides.text: Which Chinese company is the world's largest EV battery maker?

more.text: CATL.
A major maker of pouch and cylindrical cells for EVs and energy storage.

sides.text: Which Korean company is a leading EV cell maker alongside Samsung SDI?

more.text: LG Energy Solution.

sides.text: Cells for Tesla and consumer batteries

more.text: A long-time Tesla partner, with cylindrical cells made at Tesla's Nevada Gigafactory.

sides.text: Which company partners with Tesla on cylindrical cells in Nevada?

more.text: Panasonic.
Makes both vehicles and batteries, including the Blade LFP battery.

sides.text: Which carmaker also makes the Blade LFP battery?

more.text: BYD.
Makes EV and energy storage cells, with prismatic and cylindrical formats.

sides.text: Which Samsung business unit makes lithium-ion cells?

more.text: Samsung SDI.
Founded in 2018 as a joint venture of Siemens and AES. Supplies utility-scale storage systems.
Siemens and AES.
Each panel gets its own small inverter, improving shade tolerance and monitoring.

sides.text: What does Enphase make for solar panels?

more.text: Microinverters.
Panel-level power optimizers feed a central inverter.

sides.text: Which solar company is known for power optimizers?

more.text: SolarEdge.

sides.text: Industrial automation vs grid and power

more.text: Siemens AG covers industrial automation and infrastructure. Siemens Energy, spun off in 2020, makes turbines and grid equipment.

sides.text: Which company was spun off from Siemens in 2020 for energy equipment?

more.text: Siemens Energy.
A Swedish-Swiss company that makes motors, drives, robots, and electrification products.

sides.text: Which company combines robotics, drives, and grid equipment?

more.text: ABB.
A French company supplying low-voltage distribution, building automation, and data center power.

sides.text: Which French company is a leader in energy management?

more.text: Schneider Electric.

sides.text: Energy business spun from GE in 2024

more.text: Makes gas and wind turbines and grid equipment.

sides.text: Which company did GE spin off in April 2024 for energy products?

more.text: GE Vernova.

sides.text: Power and cooling for data centers

more.text: Supply power distribution, UPS, and thermal systems for facilities.

sides.text: Which type of facility depends heavily on UPS and cooling from Vertiv?

more.text: Data centers.
Materials are concentrated in a few regions, so supply risk and price swings affect cell cost. LFP avoids nickel and cobalt.

sides.text: Which lithium-ion chemistry avoids nickel and cobalt?

more.text: LFP.
Lower cost and good cold performance, but lower energy density than lithium-ion.

sides.text: What element replaces lithium in sodium-ion cells?

more.text: Sodium.
Aim for higher energy density and safety. Manufacturing and durability challenges remain.

sides.text: What replaces the liquid electrolyte in a solid-state battery?

more.text: A solid electrolyte.
Flow batteries (vanadium) store energy in tanks of liquid electrolyte. Pumped hydro stores water uphill and holds most of the world's grid storage capacity.

sides.text: Which storage technology holds most grid storage capacity today?

more.text: Pumped hydro.
Charging connector standards differ by region. NACS, from Tesla, was adopted by many carmakers in North America.

sides.text: Which connector standard did Tesla originate?

more.text: NACS.
Independent operators balance supply and demand in their regions and run electricity markets.

sides.text: Which operator manages most of the Texas grid?

more.text: ERCOT.
Supplies base stations and core networks to mobile operators worldwide.

sides.text: Which Swedish company is a major supplier of mobile network equipment?

more.text: Ericsson.
Bought Alcatel-Lucent in 2016. Supplies radio access, fixed networks, and optical gear.
Nokia.
One of the largest telecom equipment makers, with its own chip design arm, HiSilicon.

sides.text: Which company owns the chip design unit HiSilicon?

more.text: Huawei.
A leading supplier of enterprise and carrier networking equipment.

sides.text: Which company is best known for routers and switches?

more.text: Cisco.
Operated by SpaceX. Thousands of satellites at low altitude give lower latency than geostationary links.
Low Earth orbit.
3GPP defines LTE and 5G. IEEE 802.11 defines Wi-Fi, and the Wi-Fi Alliance certifies interoperability. The Bluetooth SIG governs Bluetooth.
3GPP.
Spun off from Agilent in 2014. Agilent had itself been spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 1999.

sides.text: From which company was Keysight spun off?

more.text: Agilent (which came from HP).
A long-established oscilloscope maker, now part of Fortive.

sides.text: Which company is famous for oscilloscopes and belongs to Fortive?

more.text: Tektronix.
Known for spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and wireless test equipment.

sides.text: Which German company makes RF test equipment such as spectrum analyzers?

more.text: Rohde & Schwarz.
Trusted for multimeters and industrial test tools. Part of Fortive.

sides.text: Which brand is famous for rugged multimeters?

more.text: Fluke.
Offer affordable oscilloscopes, generators, and power supplies popular with hobbyists and small labs.

sides.text: Which kind of user favors Rigol and Siglent?

more.text: Hobbyists and cost-conscious labs.
Acquired by Emerson in 2023. Known for data acquisition and graphical programming.

sides.text: Which software is National Instruments known for?

more.text: LabVIEW.
Widely used for signal processing, control design, and model-based development.
MathWorks.
Publishes journals and standards, including 802.3 (Ethernet), 802.11 (Wi-Fi), and 754 (floating point).

sides.text: Which organization maintains the Ethernet and Wi-Fi standards?

more.text: IEEE.
Sets international standards for electrical, electronic, and related technologies, including safety and EMC.

sides.text: Which organization sets international electrotechnical standards?

more.text: The IEC.
Publishes the DDR, LPDDR, and many other chip standards.

sides.text: Which body publishes the DDR memory standards?

more.text: JEDEC.

sides.text: US radio spectrum and emissions regulator

more.text: Part 15 limits unintentional radiators like electronic devices. Devices usually need FCC authorization before sale.

sides.text: Which agency regulates electromagnetic emissions of devices in the US?

more.text: The FCC.
Underwriters Laboratories tests products for safety. A UL mark is often required by retailers and codes.

sides.text: Which organization is known for safety certification marks in the US?

more.text: UL.

sides.text: NFPA 70: US wiring and installation rules

more.text: Updated every three years. Local jurisdictions adopt and amend it.

sides.text: Which code governs electrical installation in the US?

more.text: The National Electrical Code (NEC, NFPA 70).
The International Telecommunication Union allocates spectrum and sets telecom standards.

sides.text: Which UN agency coordinates global radio spectrum?

more.text: The ITU.
The USB Implementers Forum publishes specifications, including USB-C and Power Delivery, and certifies devices.

sides.text: Which organization governs the USB standard?

more.text: USB-IF.
RoHS restricts hazardous substances such as lead. CE marking declares conformity with EU safety, health, and environmental requirements.
Hazardous substances such as lead in electronics.
IPC publishes standards such as IPC-A-610 for assembly acceptability and IPC-2221 for PCB design.

sides.text: Which body publishes PCB assembly acceptability standards?

more.text: IPC.

sides.text: Safety standard for audio, video, and ICT equipment

more.text: Hazard-based safety standard that replaced IEC 60950-1 and IEC 60065 for many products.

sides.text: Which standard replaced IEC 60950-1 for IT equipment safety?

more.text: EMS companies assemble products for brands. Many handle design, sourcing, and logistics as well.
Manufacture and assemble electronics for other brands.
Engineering validation proves the design works, design validation proves it meets specs and standards, and production validation proves the line can build it reliably.

sides.text: Which stage proves the manufacturing line can build the product reliably?

more.text: PVT (production validation test).
Products usually need EMC, safety, and radio approvals (FCC, CE, UL) before they can be sold.

sides.text: What must most electronics pass before being sold?

more.text: Regulatory compliance testing and certification.

sides.text: Lead times, counterfeits, and single sources

more.text: Second-source parts, trusted distributors, and design flexibility reduce risk. The 2020–2022 shortage hit automotive production hard.

sides.text: What reduces risk from a single-source component?

more.text: Qualifying a second source.

sides.text: Analog, digital, RF, power, embedded, and test

more.text: Roles include analog and mixed-signal design, FPGA and ASIC design, RF engineering, power electronics, embedded firmware, test, and field applications.

sides.text: Which role writes the firmware that runs on a device?

more.text: An embedded firmware engineer.

sides.text: Path to a professional engineer license (US)

more.text: Pass the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam, gain experience, then pass the Professional Engineer (PE) exam. Power is a common PE discipline.

sides.text: What exam comes before the PE exam in the US?

more.text: The FE (Fundamentals of Engineering) exam.
The voltaic pile stacked zinc and copper discs with brine-soaked cloth. The unit volt is named for him.

sides.text: Who invented the first chemical battery?

more.text: Alessandro Volta.
Showed current is proportional to voltage for a conductor. The ohm is named for him.

sides.text: Who discovered the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance?

more.text: Georg Ohm.
Showed that a changing magnetic field induces a voltage, the basis of generators and transformers. The farad is named for him.
Michael Faraday.
Formulated the current and voltage laws used in every circuit analysis.

sides.text: Who formulated the current and voltage laws for circuits?

more.text: Gustav Kirchhoff.
His 1865 paper "A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field" gave the equations that predict electromagnetic waves.
James Clerk Maxwell.
Generated and detected radio waves in the lab. The hertz is named for him.

sides.text: Who first demonstrated radio waves experimentally?

more.text: Heinrich Hertz.

sides.text: AC induction motor and polyphase systems

more.text: His work made practical alternating-current motors and power distribution possible. The unit of magnetic flux density is named for him.

sides.text: Who is associated with the AC induction motor?

more.text: Nikola Tesla.
Edison's early power systems (Pearl Street Station, 1882) used DC. Westinghouse promoted AC, which transformers made efficient over long distances. AC won.

sides.text: Which current type won for long-distance power distribution?

more.text: AC.
Developed practical radio communication and sent a transatlantic radio signal in 1901.

sides.text: Who is credited with the first transatlantic radio transmission?

more.text: Guglielmo Marconi.
Invented the superheterodyne receiver and wideband FM radio.
Edwin Armstrong.
His 1948 paper defined entropy and channel capacity, setting the limits of communication.
Claude Shannon.
His 1928 work on telegraph transmission underpins the sampling theorem and the Nyquist criterion.

sides.text: Who is the Nyquist sampling criterion named after?

more.text: Harry Nyquist.
Worked at Bell Labs on feedback amplifiers. Bode plots are named for him.

sides.text: Who developed the plots used to show frequency response?

more.text: Hendrik Bode.
Conceived negative feedback in 1927 at Bell Labs, enabling stable, low-distortion amplifiers.

sides.text: Who invented the negative feedback amplifier?

more.text: Harold Black.
Created the first transistor at Bell Labs in December 1947 and shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Bell Labs.
Kilby built the first IC at Texas Instruments in 1958. Noyce developed a silicon planar IC at Fairchild in 1959. Kilby won the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics.

sides.text: Who built the first integrated circuit in 1958?

more.text: Jack Kilby.
Observed in 1965 that the number of components per chip was doubling regularly. Co-founded Intel with Robert Noyce.

sides.text: Who made the observation known as Moore's law?

more.text: Gordon Moore.
Invented the one-transistor DRAM cell at IBM and described Dennard scaling in 1974.

sides.text: Who invented the one-transistor DRAM cell?

more.text: Robert Dennard.
Hoff proposed the architecture and Faggin led the chip design.

sides.text: Which Intel chip from 1971 was the first commercial microprocessor?

more.text: The Intel 4004.
Their 1980 textbook Introduction to VLSI Systems made chip design accessible beyond a few companies.

sides.text: Which textbook popularized VLSI design methodology?

more.text: Mead and Conway's Introduction to VLSI Systems.
Their RISC work and textbook shaped modern processors. They received the 2017 Turing Award.

sides.text: Who wrote the standard computer architecture textbook and shared the 2017 Turing Award?

more.text: John Hennessy and David Patterson.
Developed recursive state estimation used in navigation, control, and tracking, including the Apollo program.
Rudolf Kálmán.
Published an efficient algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform that made digital signal processing practical.

sides.text: Who published the FFT algorithm in 1965?

more.text: James Cooley and John Tukey.
Developed Hamming codes at Bell Labs, which can correct single-bit errors.
Richard Hamming.
Viterbi introduced his decoding algorithm in 1967. He and Jacobs co-founded Qualcomm, which commercialized CDMA.

sides.text: Which two people co-founded Qualcomm and pioneered CDMA?

more.text: Irwin Jacobs and Andrew Viterbi.
Shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing lithium-ion batteries. Yoshino built the first commercially viable cell.

sides.text: Which technology won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry?

more.text: Lithium-ion batteries.
Created the pure-play foundry model in 1987.
Morris Chang.
Led NVIDIA from gaming graphics to AI computing.

sides.text: Who is NVIDIA's co-founder and CEO?

more.text: Jensen Huang.
Led the effort to build an affordable computer for teaching programming.

sides.text: Who is the co-creator of the Raspberry Pi?

more.text: Eben Upton.
Helped create the open-source Arduino platform in Italy.
Massimo Banzi.

sides.text: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field

more.text: Presented the equations of electromagnetism and showed that light is an electromagnetic wave.

sides.text: Which 1865 paper showed light is an electromagnetic wave?

more.text: Maxwell's A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field.

sides.text: Which 1928 paper set the bandwidth versus signaling-rate relationship?

more.text: Nyquist's Certain Topics in Telegraph Transmission Theory.

more.text: Hartley's Transmission of Information.
Described negative feedback to reduce distortion and stabilize gain.

sides.text: Which 1934 paper described stabilized feedback amplifiers?

more.text: Harold Black's paper.

sides.text: Who defined noise figure for radio receivers?

more.text: Harald Friis.

Shannon's A Mathematical Theory of Communication.

Bardeen and Brattain's paper.

sides.text: Who wrote the 1949 theory of PN junctions and junction transistors?

more.text: William Shockley.

Hamming's Error Detecting and Error Correcting Codes.

sides.text: Which 1952 paper introduced an optimal prefix code?

more.text: Huffman's paper.

sides.text: Which 1960 paper introduced the Kalman filter?

more.text: Kalman's A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems.

Reed and Solomon's paper.

sides.text: Which 1960 paper introduced the LMS algorithm?

more.text: Widrow and Hoff's Adaptive Switching Circuits.

Robert Gallager.

sides.text: Cramming More Components onto Integrated Circuits

more.text: Observed rapid growth in components per chip, which became known as Moore's law.

sides.text: Which 1965 article became known as Moore's law?

more.text: Moore's Cramming More Components onto Integrated Circuits.

sides.text: An Algorithm for the Machine Calculation of Complex Fourier Series

more.text: Published the FFT.
Cooley and Tukey's paper.

sides.text: Error Bounds for Convolutional Codes and an Asymptotically Optimum Decoding Algorithm
